title: SB156 (2021-2022 Regular): Prohibiting the carrying of a concealed handgun in the state capitol.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Kansas) (gun-policy Stage 5, Kansas); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Kansas text (Introduced; official copy, https://www.kslegislature.gov/li_2022/b2021_22/measures/documents/sb156_00_0000.pdf)
provenance.note: As filed (introduced); the bill has no recorded vote. Struck from K.S.A. 75-7c21(a): the existing rule that an individual may carry a concealed handgun in the state capitol if not prohibited from possessing a firearm.

operative_text:
Section 2 (K.S.A. 75-7c21): (a) No individual shall carry a concealed handgun in the state capitol, except that an individual may possess a handgun in a private means of conveyance located in any structure connected to the state capitol, or any area of such structure, designated for the parking of motor vehicles.
Section 2 (K.S.A. 75-7c21): (b) This section shall not apply to: (1) A commissioned law enforcement officer; (2) a full-time salaried law enforcement officer of another state or the federal government who is carrying out official duties while in this state; (3) a law enforcement officer, as defined in K.S.A. 75-7c22, and amendments thereto, who satisfies the requirements of either K.S.A. 75-7c22(a) or (b), and amendments thereto; (4) any person summoned by any such officer to assist in making arrests or preserving the peace while actually engaged in assisting such officer; or (5) a member of the military of this state or the United States engaged in the performance of duties.
Section 1 (K.S.A. 2020 Supp. 21-6309): (4) an individual to possess a concealed handgun provided such individual is not prohibited from possessing a firearm under either federal or state law and such individual is not in possession of a concealed handgun in the state capitol in violation of K.S.A. 75-7c21, and amendments thereto.
